title: A stack of rock plates
text: The Rand Mountains are built on a thrust fault that stacks one body of rock on another. Above the Rand thrust lie quartz monzonite and gneiss, and below it lies a rock called Rand Schist. The southwestern part of that fault was later reused as a low-angle normal fault. In the middle Miocene, the Rand Detachment Fault helped stretch the northwest Mojave Desert.

s1.title: Early history and reactivation of the Rand thrust, southern California
s1.quote: The Rand thrust of the Rand Mountains in the northwestern Mojave Desert separates an upper plate of quartz monzonite and quartzofeldspathic to amphibolitic gneiss from a lower plate of metagraywacke and mafic schist (Rand Schist). ... the southwestern portion of the Rand thrust was found to have been reactivated as a low-angle normal fault after subduction.

s2.title: Middle Miocene Displacement Along the Rand Detachment Fault, Rand Mountains
s2.quote: The Rand Detachment fault in the Rand Mountains is a middle Miocene fault that facilitated extension of the northwest Mojave Desert.
